conclusions: The October 2025 record establishes that renewal and grant-funding questions were active well before the April 2026 termination vote.
Vendor statements about encryption, deletion, ownership and sharing must remain attributed claims unless corroborated by native contract, configuration, audit or deletion records.
The GIVE award and Flock contract lifecycle should remain separate accounting predicates; grant acceptance does not equal vendor expenditure.
counterarguments: An official county summary accurately records what participants said but is not itself a native Flock configuration export or independent technical audit.
The county summary links the pending Flock renewal to GIVE funding context but does not allocate the full $220,650 resolution amount to Flock.
findings: Tompkins County's official highlights say the October 7, 2025 Legislature discussion concerned a pending renewal of Flock traffic-camera technology funded through the New York State GIVE initiative.

The official summary attributes to Flock Safety representative Trevor Chandler claims that data were end-to-end encrypted, automatically deleted after 30 days, not sold or shared by Flock, and controlled for sharing by the community/customer.

The official summary attributes to Sheriff Derek Osborne the statement that federal access required proper legal process and that local data access was limited to certain New York agencies, excluding communities with agreements with ICE.
The Legislature separately approved, 9-4, a resolution accepting $220,650 to support GIVE activities in the Sheriff's and Probation departments.
The $220,650 GIVE acceptance action is not evidence that the entire award was paid to Flock or that every funded activity involved Flock.
limitations: The linked IQM2 resolution timed out during retrieval, so this pass does not assign a native resolution number or quote its adopted text.
No native contract, invoice, platform audit, sharing export, account list, credential state or deletion record was recovered in this pass.
